- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the immediate following period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion zones — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast slightly; if below, increase slightly.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in reaction to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day delay in adjusting forecast to match sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
